source.title: Combine Two Tables
source.answer:
select p.firstName, p.lastName, a.city, a.state
from Person p
left join Address a
using(personId)

document.title: Missing directory entries
document.complaint: A registered person disappeared from our people-and-address directory.
document.business_rules: The directory must display every person. Include one row for each matching address and NULL address fields when there is no match. Repeated names and address values are valid.
document.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Person (personId INTEGER, firstName TEXT(255), lastName TEXT(255));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Address (addressId INTEGER, personId INTEGER, city TEXT(255), state TEXT(255));

components.label: Application report
components.purpose: Feeds the affected report in the application.
components.query: SELECT p.firstName, p.lastName, a.city, a.state FROM Person AS p INNER JOIN Address AS a USING (personId)
components.reference_query: SELECT p.firstName, p.lastName, a.city, a.state FROM Person AS p LEFT JOIN Address AS a USING (personId)

components.label: Record summary
components.purpose: Shows how many primary records are registered.

document.fault_cause: An INNER JOIN removes unmatched records required by this report.
checkpoints: Compare the primary records with the report output.
Trace which relationships include, omit or multiply records.
An INNER JOIN removes unmatched records required by this report.

scenarios.label: Initial incident records
Boundary and cardinality records
scenarios.seed_sql: INSERT INTO Person VALUES (10,'Kai','Tan'),(20,'Kai','Tan'); INSERT INTO Address VALUES (1,10,NULL,'North'),(2,20,'East','East'),(3,20,'East','East');

alternative_repairs: SELECT p.firstName, p.lastName, a.city, a.state FROM Person AS p LEFT JOIN Address AS a USING (personId)

source.title: Customers Who Never Order
source.answer:
select name as Customers
from Customers
where id not in
    (select distinct customerId
    from Orders)

document.title: Outreach recipients look wrong
document.complaint: Our outreach list includes regular buyers and misses people who have never ordered.
document.business_rules: Show each customer with no order. A customer with one or several orders must be absent. Customers are identified by their ID, not their name.
document.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Customers (id INTEGER, name TEXT(255));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Orders (id INTEGER, customerId INTEGER);

components.label: Application report
components.purpose: Feeds the affected report in the application.
components.query: SELECT c.name AS Customers FROM Customers AS c WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Orders AS o WHERE o.customerId = c.id)
components.reference_query: SELECT c.name AS Customers FROM Customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders o WHERE o.customerId=c.id)

components.label: Record summary
components.purpose: Shows how many primary records are registered.

document.fault_cause: The existence predicate selects customers with orders instead of customers without orders.
checkpoints: Compare the primary records with the report output.
Trace which relationships include, omit or multiply records.
The existence predicate selects customers with orders instead of customers without orders.

scenarios.label: Initial incident records
Boundary and cardinality records
scenarios.seed_sql: INSERT INTO Customers VALUES (10,'Dee'),(20,'Eli'); INSERT INTO Orders VALUES (1,10),(2,10),(3,20);

alternative_repairs: SELECT c.name AS Customers FROM Customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders o WHERE o.customerId=c.id)

source.title: Employees Earning More Than Their Managers
source.answer:
select e.name as 'Employee'
from Employee m 
left join Employee e
on e.managerId = m.id
where e.salary > m.salary

document.title: Payroll alerts reach the wrong staff
document.complaint: Payroll alerts are being sent for the wrong reporting relationships.
document.business_rules: An alert belongs to an employee only when their salary is strictly greater than their own manager's salary. Equal salaries and staff without a manager do not trigger alerts.
document.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Employee (id INTEGER, name TEXT(255), salary INTEGER, managerId INTEGER);

components.label: Application report
components.purpose: Feeds the affected report in the application.
components.query: SELECT e.name AS "Employee" FROM Employee AS m LEFT JOIN Employee AS e ON e.managerId = m.id WHERE e.salary < m.salary
components.reference_query: SELECT e.name AS "Employee" FROM Employee AS m LEFT JOIN Employee AS e ON e.managerId = m.id WHERE e.salary > m.salary

components.label: Record summary
components.purpose: Shows how many primary records are registered.

document.fault_cause: The salary comparison is reversed; an employee must earn more than their own manager.
checkpoints: Compare the primary records with the report output.
Trace which relationships include, omit or multiply records.
The salary comparison is reversed; an employee must earn more than their own manager.

scenarios.label: Initial incident records

alternative_repairs: SELECT e.name AS "Employee" FROM Employee AS m LEFT JOIN Employee AS e ON e.managerId = m.id WHERE e.salary > m.salary

source.title: Replace Employee ID With The Unique Identifier
source.answer:
select unique_id, name 
from Employees e left join EmployeeUNI eu on e.id = eu.id

document.title: Identity badges are mismatched
document.complaint: The staff directory assigns a badge to the wrong employee and loses other badge mappings.
document.business_rules: Display every employee's name and their mapped unique_id, or NULL when no mapping exists. Employees.id and EmployeeUNI.id identify the same employee; unique_id is a badge identifier.
document.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Employees (id INTEGER, name TEXT(20));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS EmployeeUNI (id INTEGER, unique_id INTEGER);

components.label: Application report
components.purpose: Feeds the affected report in the application.
components.query: SELECT unique_id, name FROM Employees AS e LEFT JOIN EmployeeUNI AS eu ON e.id = eu.unique_id
components.reference_query: SELECT unique_id, name FROM Employees AS e LEFT JOIN EmployeeUNI AS eu ON e.id = eu.id

components.label: Record summary
components.purpose: Shows how many primary records are registered.

document.fault_cause: The join uses a different identifier domain, creating false matches or missing relationships.
checkpoints: Compare the primary records with the report output.
Trace which relationships include, omit or multiply records.
The join uses a different identifier domain, creating false matches or missing relationships.

scenarios.label: Initial incident records
Boundary and cardinality records
scenarios.seed_sql: INSERT INTO Employees VALUES (2,'Noor'),(3,'Uma'); INSERT INTO EmployeeUNI VALUES (2,100),(3,200);

alternative_repairs: SELECT unique_id, name FROM Employees AS e LEFT JOIN EmployeeUNI AS eu ON e.id = eu.id

source.title: Customer Who Visited but Did Not Make Any Transactions
source.answer:
select customer_id, count(visit_id) as count_no_trans
from
(
select v.visit_id, v.customer_id, t.transaction_id, t.visit_id as transaction_visit
from Visits v left join Transactions t on v.visit_id = t.visit_id) temp
where transaction_visit is null
group by customer_id

document.title: Unconverted visits vanish
document.complaint: The customer dashboard reports no visits without purchases, despite recorded visits with no transaction.
document.business_rules: For each customer with at least one visit that has no transaction, report customer_id and count_no_trans. Count visits without transactions, not transaction records; one visit can have multiple transactions.
document.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Visits (visit_id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Transactions (transaction_id INTEGER, visit_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER);

components.label: Application report
components.purpose: Feeds the affected report in the application.
components.query: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(visit_id) AS count_no_trans FROM (SELECT v.visit_id, v.customer_id, t.transaction_id, t.visit_id AS transaction_visit FROM Visits AS v INNER JOIN Transactions AS t ON v.visit_id = t.visit_id) AS temp WHERE transaction_visit IS NULL GROUP BY customer_id
components.reference_query: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(visit_id) AS count_no_trans FROM (SELECT v.visit_id, v.customer_id, t.transaction_id, t.visit_id AS transaction_visit FROM Visits AS v LEFT JOIN Transactions AS t ON v.visit_id = t.visit_id) AS temp WHERE transaction_visit IS NULL GROUP BY customer_id

source.title: Product Sales Analysis I
source.answer:
select product_name, year, price
from Sales s left join Product p on s.product_id = p.product_id

document.title: Revenue is attributed incorrectly
document.complaint: The sales dashboard shows missing revenue or attributes it to an unrelated product.
document.business_rules: Report total quantity times price for each product with sales, grouping by product identity and name. Sales.product_id references Product.product_id; sale_id identifies a sale, not a product.
document.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Sales (sale_id INTEGER, product_id INTEGER, year INTEGER, quantity INTEGER, price INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Product (product_id INTEGER, product_name TEXT(10));

components.label: Application report
components.purpose: Feeds the affected report in the application.
components.query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(s.quantity*s.price) AS revenue FROM Sales s INNER JOIN Product p ON s.sale_id=p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id,p.product_name
components.reference_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(s.quantity*s.price) AS revenue FROM Sales s INNER JOIN Product p ON s.product_id=p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id,p.product_name

components.purpose: Shows how many primary records are registered.

checkpoints: Compare the primary records with the report output.
Trace which relationships include, omit or multiply records.
